Confidence intervals for cross-validated metrics

Source: R/cv_uncertainty.R
cv_ci.Rd

Computes per-learner confidence intervals for each metric column in a per-fold metrics data.frame. Supports the standard normal/t approach and the Nadeau-Bengio (2003) corrected variance for repeated K-fold CV.

Usage

cv_ci(
  metrics_df,
  level = 0.95,
  method = c("nadeau_bengio", "normal"),
  n_train = NULL,
  n_test = NULL,
  folds_per_repeat = NULL
)

Arguments

metrics_df

A LeakFit or a LeakTune (recommended: fold sizes, folds per repeat and repeated test sets are then taken from the object's splits), or a data.frame with columns fold, learner, and one or more numeric metric columns, such as fit@metrics. An optional character column test_set identifies each fold's test set: folds sharing a test set (repeats that re-use the same partition) are averaged and counted once.

level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

method

"nadeau_bengio" (default) or "normal". "normal" treats folds as independent and is far too narrow for cross-validation (about 37% coverage of a nominal 95% interval for repeated 5-fold CV in simulation); it is kept for comparison.

n_train

Average number of training samples per fold. Used only when method = "nadeau_bengio". NULL to use fallback variance.

n_test

Average number of test samples per fold. Used only when method = "nadeau_bengio". Without n_train and n_test the correction cannot be applied: a warning is issued and the uncorrected variance var / K is used.

folds_per_repeat

Number of folds in one CV repeat (e.g. 5 for 5-fold CV repeated 10 times). Used only when method = "nadeau_bengio" to set the degrees of freedom. The resulting intervals are slightly conservative in simulation (about 98% coverage at the 95% level for repeated 5-fold CV). Intervals are not clipped to a metric's range (e.g. an AUC bound can exceed 1).

Value

A data.frame with learner and, for each metric, columns <metric>_mean, <metric>_sd, <metric>_ci_lo, and <metric>_ci_hi.

Details

Fold metrics from cross-validation are correlated: training sets overlap, and repeats re-partition the same data. "normal" ignores this (sd / sqrt(K) over all folds) and is too narrow for repeated CV. "nadeau_bengio" inflates the variance to (1/K + n_test/n_train) * var and uses a t reference on folds_per_repeat - 1 degrees of freedom (calibrated degrees of freedom, Bouckaert 2003): repeats sharpen the estimate but add no independent information. Without folds_per_repeat all folds are treated as one repeat.
